obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card data compromise (contractual)
citation: Merchant agreement with the acquiring bank (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10.1 (N81-R03)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of card data, for example POS malware at AC stores, a common point of purchase notice, or a tampered PIN pad
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspecting a compromise (merchant agreement term)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

obligation: Card brand compromise reporting: Visa worked example (contractual)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Sections A.1-A.3 and A.5; Visa Core Rules 10.3.1.2. Card brand rules applied through the acquirer, not law. If the business accepts American Express, the DSOP (April 2026, Section 3) requires notice to American Express within 72 hours of discovery. Mastercard and Discover rules not verified
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a system that stores, processes or transmits it
deadline: Tell the acquirer immediately (A.3.1). Make sure the event is reported to Visa within 3 calendar days of the suspicion or confirmation (A.1.1), then send the incident report within 3 calendar days of that notice (A.2.1). If Visa requires a PCI Forensic Investigator, retain one within 5 business days (A.5.1.1)
notify: Acquirer; Visa Global Risk Investigations, through the acquirer. Other brands as the acquirer directs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a case is opened; Mastercard and Discover rules were not verified
clock_starts: Suspicion or confirmation of the compromise

obligation: Manufacturer A, B, or C notice of suspected customer data incident (contractual)
trigger: Suspected incident involving customer data or devices handled under a program (for example theft of AC ticket data for Manufacturer C repairs, or a technician copying device content)
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspicion (program agreement term)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

obligation: SL-1 client notice (contractual)
citation: SL-1 client master agreements, security exhibit (fictional term)
trigger: Incident affecting SL-1 claim data or the claims API
deadline: Within 48 hours of confirmation; updates every 72 hours until closed
notify: Each affected protection plan administrator or carrier
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for affected SL-1 clients - contractual

obligation: SL-2 client notice (contractual)
trigger: Incident affecting SL-2 client devices, asset records, or sanitization records
deadline: Within 72 hours of confirmation
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for affected SL-2 clients - contractual

obligation: Business associate breach notice to SL-2 health care clients
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI on an SL-2 health care client device or record
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery; most BAAs set a shorter term (see the BAA abstract)
notify: The covered entity client, with the identity of each affected individual where possible
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for the 38 SL-2 health care clients only
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any workforce member or agent (164.410(a)(2))

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; use the carrier breach hotline before hiring vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

obligation: State data breach notification (all affected states)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48) (N81-R02)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example without unreasonable delay, or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - customers in all 44 states and DC where stores operate, plus mail-in customers elsewhere; counsel applies each state's law from its state matrix

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Unauthorized access of data in electronic form containing personal information of Florida residents. Personal information includes an email address or user name with a password, a name with a card number and any required security or access code, and a name with medical, biometric, or geolocation information (501.171(1)(g)). Good-faith employee access for a business purpose is not a breach (501.171(1)(a))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; 15 more days if good cause is given in writing to the Department within 30 days (this extension applies only to notice to individuals)
notify: Each affected Florida resident by mail or email ((4)(d)) with the content in (4)(e)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected for exported legacy tickets with email and password pairs; counsel decides for card data and device content
clock_starts: Determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (no extension for this notice). Content listed in (3)(b)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Florida law enforcement delay (worked example)
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines in writing that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in writing
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Florida no-notice determination (worked example)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document in writing, keep at least 5 years, and provide to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Possible for contained incidents (for example a single technician case with no copies); counsel decides

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice (worked example; inbound and outbound)
trigger: Inbound: a vendor that maintains personal information for the company has a breach. Outbound: the company has a breach of data it maintains for an SL-1 or SL-2 client that is a covered entity
deadline: No later than 10 days after the determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred, with the information the covered entity needs to notify
notify: Inbound: the company. Outbound: the client covered entity
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - both directions
clock_starts: Determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
owner: Director of Third-Party Risk Management (inbound); Vice President, Claims Fulfillment and Vice President, Enterprise Services (outbound)

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incident)
trigger: The disclosure committee determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination. The determination itself must be made without unreasonable delay after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant
clock_starts: Materiality determination (date and time recorded in the minutes)

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 delay for national security or public safety
trigger: The U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Delay only for the period the Attorney General specifies; request through outside counsel to the Department of Justice
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - rarely expected for this incident type

obligation: SEC Form 8-K/A update
trigger: Information required by Item 1.05 was not determined or was unavailable at the time of the initial filing
deadline: Counsel confirms the timing of any amendment under the release when the information is determined or becomes available
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant
clock_starts: When the information is determined or becomes available

obligation: SEC Regulation S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report (10-K): describe risk management, strategy, and governance; describe whether risks from cybersecurity threats, including previous incidents, have materially affected or are reasonably likely to materially affect the company
deadline: With the annual report on Form 10-K
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any ransom or extortion payment (for example a demand to delete stolen ticket data)
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a demand is made. All U.S. persons; strict liability

obligation: Report to law enforcement
trigger: Criminal compromise of card data or customer accounts; theft of customer data by a workforce member
deadline: As soon as practical (target day 0-2); coordinate with counsel, the PFI, and the acquirer
notify: FBI (IC3) or U.S. Secret Service field office; local police for insider theft
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). Proposed scope includes critical infrastructure entities above the SBA size standard; recheck applicability when the final rule is published
clock_starts: n/a until a final rule takes effect

obligation: HIPAA covered entity notices to individuals, HHS, and media
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI at a covered entity
deadline: n/a for the company
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is not a covered entity; for SL-2 it notifies the covered entity client (164.410 row above), and the client makes these notices

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event
trigger: Notification event at a financial institution involving 500 or more consumers
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company does not extend credit to consumers and is not a financial institution under Part 314 (P03 screen)

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a Kaspersky covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
